- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward.
- After a sharp spike in price or sentiment, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show upward trend, forecast should not continue rising beyond 10–15% above recent high.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model tends to smooth out extremes; use sentiment-weighted moving average to correct for lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the window; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to correct; add a “reversion buffer” of 1–3% below peak for 3–5 days post-spike.
